title: Holding the door for someone way too far away

narrator.style: clear, clean, crisp studio voice with precise articulation, smooth, not breathy, not raspy; dry deadpan narrator, slightly unimpressed, natural pace

theo.style: clear, clean voice, not breathy, not raspy; cheeky young guy roasting his friend, trying not to laugh

lines.say: Way behind you. Like, different zip code behind you.
But your mom raised you right. So you hold the door.
Big mistake. Now it's a contract.
They see you. You see them. Nobody can back out now.
So they do the jog. The little fake thank-you jog.
It's not faster. It's just walking, but sweatier.
Your arm is shaking. This is the most eye contact you've had all year.
And of course, Theo walks by.
Bro. You look like a doorman nobody tips. Absolute clown.
Thirty seconds later, they finally arrive.
They smile at you. And they say:
Oh, sorry. I wasn't going in.
You held that door for absolutely fucking nothing.
Then a pigeon walks in. Doesn't even say thanks.
Theo walks in too. Eating a croissant. Also no thanks, the little shit.
You finally let go of the door.
